title: Golden Gate Highlands: Massospondylus nesting site, South Africa
summary: At Rooidraai in Golden Gate Highlands National Park, a road cut about 25 metres long holds ten clutches of Massospondylus eggs, one with at least 34 eggs, some with embryos, in Early Jurassic rock about 190 million years old. Reported in 2012 as the oldest known dinosaur nesting site, it lies in lake-margin flood-basin deposits and suggests the animals returned to nest repeatedly.

uncertainty.note: The University of Toronto release gives a rounded '190 million years old' with no error; the PNAS paper gives only 'Early Jurassic'. The ±5 million year range is an editorial allowance for the rounding. The site was assigned to the upper Elliot Formation, not the Clarens Formation.

beats.caption: Early Jurassic muddy siltstones of the upper Elliot Formation record a seasonally dry flood basin and lake margin, with repeated flooding and drying.
Ten Massospondylus egg clutches lie at several levels of a roadside cut; the fullest has at least 34 eggs, some with embryos.
Judged the oldest known dinosaur nesting site, it indicates the animals returned to the same spot repeatedly and nested in groups.
